_**User (2026-04-17 09:20:32Z)**_

I want to modify the way that the program determines how many chapters are in a series.
I want to determine the number of chapters using the Ch number that is displayed in the Series chapters list.
Based on the highest number that number will equal the total number of chapters. So, if the Ch number in the list is 25, that number should be displayed on the Series card in the upper right corner as the total number of chapters. And in the position of the number of unread chapters, if no chapters have been read, should equal the same as total number of chapters.
If the Ch number has a number after the decimal point (example 35.2) then round down to the whole number for the total number of chapters (example 35.2 equals 35, also 35.9 equals 35).
Do not change the way Ch is displayed in the list.
When it come to calculating the number of unread chapters start with the number equal to the total number of chapters. Then subtract chapters only when the number of chapters changes by a whole chapter. So, if I have ten chapters and I read a total of three chapters the remaining count should be seven.
If a chapter has multiple parts (example 35 and 35.5 and 35.8) only when the chapter numbers changes to 36 can a chapter be considered fully completed.
Examples: 
1)	You read chapter 10 and there are no other chapters with a 10 then chapter 10 is complete.
2)	You read chapter 10.2 and 10.5 and there are no other chapters with a 10 then chapter 10 is complete.
3)	You read chapter 10.2 and 10.5 and there is another unread chapter 10.8 then chapter 10 is not complete.
Use methods to repair and optimize the code.
Make sure any changes do not cause program errors. And do not cause errors in Lint and Release.

+ * multiple parts (e.g. 47.1, 47.2).
  * @param chapterList the list of chapters to calculate from (usually all of a series' chapters)
  * @returns the number of unread whole chapters

What was wrong
- The UI was still relying on stored series unread values in several places.
- Even with improved chapter math, stale stored values could still show the wrong unread count.

What I changed
1. Unread counting now enforces whole-chapter grouping:
- `apps/desktop/src/renderer/util/comparison.ts#L83`
- Each whole chapter number contributes at most one unread.
- If any part of a whole chapter is unread, that whole chapter is unread once.

2. Library metadata now computes both total and unread from live chapter data (with chapter-language filtering):
- `apps/desktop/src/renderer/util/librarySeriesMetadata.ts#L1`
- Added unreadChapters to metadata and compute it using grouped unread logic.
- Keeps total and unread derived from the same chapter set.

3. Library filtering/sorting now uses computed unread, not stale persisted values:
- `apps/desktop/src/renderer/components/library/Library.tsx#L1`
- Unread and Finished filters now use computed unread.
- Unread sort now uses computed unread.

4. Series card unread display now uses computed unread:
- `apps/desktop/src/renderer/components/library/LibraryGrid.tsx#L69`

5. List view unread badge now also uses computed unread:
- `apps/desktop/src/renderer/components/library/LibraryList.tsx#L1`

Why this fixes your 47.1/47.2 case
- 47.1 and 47.2 are grouped into whole chapter 47.
- 47 is counted as unread if any part is unread.
- That group contributes exactly one unread count.
- So 47.1 read + 47.2 unread now yields unread = 1 for chapter 47.

The `series.numberUnread` stored on disk was calculated by the **round-2 gap algorithm** which counted gaps (chapters 1-45 + 47.x → gap = 1 missing chapter 46 → `47 - 45 completed = 2`). That stale value of 2 is what the badge shows whenever `chapterMetadata?.unreadChapters` is somehow undefined **or** when the metadata was built from an older compiled bundle.

The definitive fix is:
1. Strip every fallback to stale `series.numberUnread` from the badge/filter/sort — always use only the freshly computed metadata value  
2. Add a one-time startup migration in `App.tsx` that recomputes `numberUnread` for every series from live chapter data — this purges any stale persisted values from previous algorithm versions  

These two changes together eliminate the root cause regardless of which stored value came from an older build.

2. **Library.tsx / LibraryGrid.tsx / LibraryList.tsx** — remove every fallback to `series.numberUnread` so the badge always shows the freshly computed value, never the stale stored one
